# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v1 c9 P45](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0045)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Widowed  <sub>[v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000), [v2 c26 P3](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0003)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife and community organizer  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Rachel  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Rachel Lynde  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a stout woman who waddles when she walks and weighs roughly two hundred pounds. She keeps a sharp, all-seeing eye on everything passing through Lynde's Hollow from her kitchen window.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c38 P30](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0030)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a capable, notable housewife who manages her own affairs and her neighbors' with equal vigor. She prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, often being outspoken and blunt to the point of being considered meddlesome. Despite her critical, pessimistic tendencies and knack for dropping unsettling remarks, she has a kind, charitable heart, never hesitating to help the poor or care for the sick.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007), [v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, diligently managing her home, church auxiliaries, and the Sewing Circle while keeping close watch over her neighbors. When the Cuthberts decided to adopt an orphan, she openly disapproved of the risky venture and later insulted young Anne Shirley's looks, prompting a fiery outburst from the girl. After Anne apologized, Mrs. Rachel quickly forgave her and grew to like her, eventually becoming a strong advocate for Anne's education and career. Over the years, Mrs. Rachel actively participated in local events, including the church bazaar and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society's efforts. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she nursed him devotedly until his death. Facing the necessity of selling her mortgaged farm, she accepted Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables, where she set up her quarters in the former spare room and helped care for the Keith twins.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P25](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0025), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034), [v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v2 c14 P5](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0005), [v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000), [v2 c26 P15](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0015), [v2 c26 P21](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0021)_

## Background by volume

- Raised ten children and buried two  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030)</sub>
- Lived in Lynde's Hollow as a long-time Avonlea resident  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v2 c26 P17](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0017)</sub>
- Staunch Liberal in political affiliation  <sub>[v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v1 c18 P41](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0041)</sub>

## Quotes

> There are plenty of people, in Avonlea and out of it, who can attend closely to their neighbors’ business by dint of neglecting their own; but Mrs. Rachel Lynde was one of those capable creatures who can manage their own concerns and those of other folks into the bargain.  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

> Well, I see that I’ll have to be very careful what I say after this, Marilla, since the fine feelings of orphans, brought from goodness knows where, have to be considered before anything else.  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030)</sub>

> I did make a mistake in judging Anne, but it weren’t no wonder, for an odder, unexpecteder witch of a child there never was in this world, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>

> You’ve got as much education now as a woman can be comfortable with. I don’t believe in girls going to college with the men and cramming their heads full of Latin and Greek and all that nonsense.  <sub>[v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)</sub>

> I’m not an encyclopedia, neither am I a Philadelphia lawyer.  <sub>[v2 c26 P29](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0029)</sub>
